cf.title: Add PAM Tests and Option For Custom PAM Config Location

input.subject: Add PAM Tests and Option For Custom PAM Config Location

verdict_reasoning: PAM test coverage is a sound goal and no objection to it survived. The open point is the permanent pg_hba.conf option that the commit message says was "mostly implemented for the sake of testing". already-exists-1 asks why a test-only redirect such as pam_wrapper is not enough, and demand-1 finds no production user asking for pamconfdir. The list should settle that choice before code review.

brief.title: PAM authentication tests and pamconfdir option in pg_hba.conf
brief.problem: Postgres has no tests for PAM authentication. The author thinks none exist because a test would need root to write /etc/pam.d, or a test environment set up by hand. The commit message adds that sites where DBAs have no root access could use a custom PAM configuration directory.
brief.proposed_design: A new pg_hba.conf option, pamconfdir, makes the server call pam_start_confdir (linux-pam 1.4.0 and later) instead of pam_start. Configure and meson probe for that function, and builds without it leave the option out. A new TAP suite in src/test/pam writes a temporary PAM configuration that uses pam_permit and pam_exec, and runs only when PG_TEST_EXTRA includes pam.
user_visible_surface: New pg_hba.conf option pamconfdir for the pam method, present only when built against a PAM that has pam_start_confdir.
New PG_TEST_EXTRA value pam that enables the src/test/pam TAP suite.
New build-time symbol HAVE_PAM_START_CONFDIR in pg_config.h.
author_claims: Postgres has no PAM tests today, and this suite adds coverage without root or a hand-prepared environment.
pamconfdir is useful outside tests, for example where DBAs are not allowed root access.
Builds against older PAM work unchanged; the author built on NixOS with PAM 1.3.1 and 1.7.2, using both make and meson.
Testing only with pamconfdir set is acceptable because the code paths are mostly the same as with the default directory.
brief.thread_state: Brian Cosgrove reviewed v2 and found 5 of 26 assertions failing under meson because of a wrong log path; he also asked for pamconfdir in pg_hba_file_rules, pam in CI and regress.sgml, and a meson fix so frontend tools do not link PAM. The author has not replied to that review.
unclear: The proposal does not say whether the server checks that the pamconfdir directory exists or who may write to it, so its security effect is not discussed.
The proposal does not say what happens when pg_hba.conf names pamconfdir on a build without pam_start_confdir: an error, a warning, or silent ignore.
The default PAM path, used without pamconfdir, gets no test coverage, and the material does not say whether that gap is acceptable.
The tests cannot run on FreeBSD or macOS, and the material does not say whether buildfarm or CI coverage on Linux is enough.

objections.title: pam_wrapper already allows rootless PAM tests without a new pg_hba option
objections.failure_scenario: Postgres ships pamconfdir as a permanent pg_hba.conf option that exists only on some builds. The new suite runs only through pam_start_confdir, so a regression in the plain pam_start path that production servers use still passes CI. The project then supports a production option that was added mostly for tests.
objections.argument: The pam_wrapper library from the cwrap project preloads into a process and redirects PAM service lookup to a test directory, with no root. A suite built on it would test the unchanged pam_start path, which message #1 accepts as untested. The commit message says the option was "mostly implemented for the sake of testing" and gives non-root DBAs as a secondary use, with no field report. The cost of pam_wrapper is one more optional test dependency and LD_PRELOAD limits on some platforms.
objections.author_must_show: Why is a server-side pamconfdir option better than running the tests under pam_wrapper, which also covers the default pam_start path?

critic.reasoning: pam_wrapper exists and redirects PAM service lookup without root, and the thread does not discuss it. The author's own statement that the option was mostly added for testing makes a test-only alternative a fair question.

objections.title: User-facing pamconfdir option justified mainly by test needs
objections.failure_scenario: Postgres ships pamconfdir as a permanent pg_hba.conf option, and every later release must document and support it. If few production sites set it, the project keeps a security-relevant knob, chosen per build, that serves mostly its own test suite. A committer would find this out only after removal is no longer possible.
objections.argument: The commit message says the option "was mostly implemented for the sake of testing". Its only production case is DBAs without root, given in one sentence with no field report. Such a DBA still needs a sysadmin to install PAM modules and grant access to credential stores, and a one-time /etc/pam.d/postgresql file covers that today. Message #3 asks for pg_hba_file_rules support, which grows the surface, but no one in the thread asks for the option itself.
objections.author_must_show: Which production sites need a non-default PAM directory per pg_hba line, and why can their sysadmin not install a file in /etc/pam.d once?

critic.reasoning: The only production case is one sentence in the commit message, and no user in the thread asks for the option. This is a show-demand point, and evidence of sites that need a non-default PAM directory would answer it.

other_surviving.title: pamconfdir exists only on some builds; behaviour elsewhere is undefined
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A DBA sets pamconfdir on a Rocky 9 primary, then copies pg_hba.conf to a standby or a new host built against PAM 1.3.1 (Rocky 8). Depending on how unknown options are handled, the reload fails or the option is ignored and PAM reads /etc/pam.d. The DBA finds out at failover, when logins fail or follow a different policy.
other_surviving.argument: Message #1 says the option is removed from builds without pam_start_confdir. Neither the documentation hunk nor the thread says what the server does when it reads the option on such a build. Postgres has an existing pattern for this: hba.c rejects options for unsupported build features with a clear error. The proposal does not say whether it follows that pattern.
other_surviving.author_must_show: What does a server built without pam_start_confdir do when pg_hba.conf contains pamconfdir, and does that match how hba.c handles other build-dependent options?

critic.reasoning: The material says ifdef gates remove the functionality, but not whether the gate covers option parsing in hba.c. If it does not, an older build could accept pamconfdir and read /etc/pam.d without any error.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: New hba option missing from pg_hba_file_rules and the manual
other_surviving.failure_scenario: An administrator checks the active rules with select * from pg_hba_file_rules and does not see pamconfdir. They assume PAM reads /etc/pam.d, while the server uses another directory. Audits and troubleshooting therefore rely on output that is incomplete.
other_surviving.argument: Message #3 reports that get_hba_options() in hbafuncs.c does not emit pamconfdir. It also reports that regress.sgml does not list the new PG_TEST_EXTRA value. The author has not replied to that review, so neither gap is resolved. Every other hba option appears in pg_hba_file_rules.options, so leaving this one out would be an inconsistency that users can see.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Will the next version show pamconfdir in pg_hba_file_rules.options and document the pam PG_TEST_EXTRA value in the manual?

critic.reasoning: Message #3 reports that pg_hba_file_rules.options omits pamconfdir, and the author has not replied. The regress.sgml part is documentation detail and should not carry weight.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

refuted.title: Permanent pg_hba.conf option added mainly to make tests possible
refuted.failure_scenario: Once released, pamconfdir appears in production pg_hba.conf files and the project has to support it indefinitely. The postgres OS account can then set authentication policy that today only root controls in /etc/pam.d. Sites learn about this shift only after it is in use.
refuted.argument: The commit message says the option "was mostly implemented for the sake of testing". Its only production use case is one sentence about DBAs without root, with no field report behind it. A test-only way to redirect PAM configuration, such as an LD_PRELOAD wrapper like pam_wrapper, would get the coverage without adding user-facing configuration. The proposal does not say why such an approach was rejected.
refuted.author_must_show: Which production users need pamconfdir today, and why can the tests not redirect PAM configuration without a new pg_hba.conf option?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-1 (no shown production demand) and already-exists-1 (pam_wrapper alternative). Its security point is weak, because the server's OS user already controls pg_hba.conf and can set trust.

refuted.title: pamconfdir has no ownership or permission check on the PAM directory
refuted.failure_scenario: A DBA without root sets pamconfdir to a group-writable or shared directory. Another local account adds a service file using pam_permit or pam_exec, and every role on that pg_hba.conf line can then log in without a valid password. No one notices until an audit or an incident.
refuted.argument: The pamconfdir file decides which modules run and whether authentication succeeds, so it carries the same weight as pg_hba.conf. Postgres refuses to start when ssl_key_file has loose permissions, and the proposal gives this directory no comparable check. The commit message presents the option for sites where DBAs have no root, which are the sites most likely to pick a non-root-owned directory. The brief lists the missing existence and writer checks as unresolved, and messages #1 to #3 do not cover them.
refuted.author_must_show: Will the server reject a pamconfdir, or a service file in it, that users other than root or the server's OS user can write, like the ssl_key_file check?

critic.reasoning: The scenario needs the administrator to choose a directory that others can write. Postgres makes no such check for hba_file, ident_file or pg_hba.conf include files, which carry the same weight, so the option follows existing practice.

refuted.title: User-facing pg_hba option added mainly to serve a test suite
refuted.failure_scenario: A DBA without root adds pamconfdir=/home/postgres/pam.d to pg_hba.conf, following the new documentation. Authentication policy now lives in a directory the server's OS user can write, outside the usual PAM controls. Moving the same pg_hba.conf to a FreeBSD, macOS or older-PAM build stops it from loading, and the DBA finds out at reload or restart.
refuted.argument: The commit message says the option "was mostly implemented for the sake of testing". Its only production case is DBAs who lack root, and the thread shows no user asking for that. Once shipped, pamconfdir is a permanent pg_hba.conf option. It exists only on some builds, and the proposal does not say whether other builds reject it, warn, or ignore it. A committer would likely ask for the production case to be argued on its own merits, or for the tests to reach PAM without a new user-facing setting.
refuted.author_must_show: Which users need a non-default PAM directory in production, and what does a pg_hba.conf naming pamconfdir do on a build without pam_start_confdir?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-1 for the missing production demand, and of standards-compat-2 for the behaviour on builds without pam_start_confdir.

refuted.title: Opt-in suite skips the default pam_start path and does not run in CI
refuted.failure_scenario: A later change breaks PAM authentication in the default pam_start branch, the one every production setup without pamconfdir uses. The new suite passes, because it runs only with pamconfdir set. It also runs only when PG_TEST_EXTRA includes pam, which CI does not set, so users report the regression after release.
refuted.argument: Message #1 accepts testing only the pamconfdir branch because "the code paths are mostly the same", so the coverage gap is deliberate. Message #3 shows 5 of 26 assertions failing under meson, and notes that the CI Linux job builds with --with-pam yet skips these tests. A suite that runs nowhere by default tends to break unnoticed. The visible thread has no committer who knows the authentication code, and the author has not answered the review.
refuted.author_must_show: Which CI or buildfarm jobs will run this suite by default, and how does it catch a regression in the pam_start path used without pamconfdir?

critic.reasoning: The scenario describes today's state, where PAM has no tests at all, so the patch does not make it worse. The PG_TEST_EXTRA gate copies the ldap and kerberos suites, and the CI and log-path points are test-level items already raised in message #3.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: The new option should appear in the pg_hba_file_rules.options column, and message #3 reports that it does not.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch touches src/include/libpq/hba.h to carry the new pamconfdir value.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: pamconfdir changes which directory supplies the PAM policy that decides authentication.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: A permanent pg_hba.conf option, two build probes and a Linux-only opt-in test suite depend on a linux-pam function.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: pam_wrapper may give rootless PAM tests without a server option, and the thread does not discuss it.

questions: Why is a server-side pamconfdir option better than running the tests under pam_wrapper, which also covers the default pam_start path?
Which production sites need a non-default PAM directory per pg_hba.conf line, and why can their sysadmin not install a file in /etc/pam.d once?
What does a server built without pam_start_confdir do when pg_hba.conf contains pamconfdir: error, warning, or silent ignore?
Will the next version show pamconfdir in pg_hba_file_rules.options, as message #3 asks?
Does the server check that the pamconfdir directory exists when it loads pg_hba.conf, or does a wrong path show up only at login?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows the client authentication code (auth.c, hba.c) and the configure and meson probes would have to own it. The visible thread has the author and one reviewer.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a permanent pg_hba.conf option tied to a linux-pam function, present only on some builds. The test suite runs only on Linux and only with PG_TEST_EXTRA=pam.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted a second version six days after the first without being asked. The review in message #3, from 2026-09-22, has no reply yet.

priority.reason: The patch is about 20 KiB and touches auth.c, hba.c and the build files, so review is cheap. The value is test coverage for PAM users, but the choice between a permanent pg_hba.conf option and a test-only redirect should be settled first.

provisional_note: Without the code, it could not be checked whether the ifdef gate covers option parsing in hba.c, so behaviour on builds without pam_start_confdir is unknown. The two level 2 objections that survived (standards-compat-2, standards-compat-3) were not evaluated.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow cluster owner to bypass authentication
precedents_retrieved.summary: A connection over a Unix-domain socket whose local effective OS user is the same as the server's effective user is accepted at once, without checking pg_hba.conf, and an option turns this off. The patch was meant as a first step before changing the initdb default authentication to md5 or SCRAM for both local and host connections.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut withdrew it and David Steele marked it Returned with feedback, because the discussion of a new default security configuration did not reach consensus. Stephen Frost objected that bypassing pg_hba.conf skips safeguards and audit trails, and that getpeerid() does not show the client has the same access as the server. Tom Lane and Stephen Frost preferred building this behavior into username maps (pg_ident.conf) instead.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It appears that the whole discussion of what a new default security
configuration could or should be hasn't really moved to a new consensus,
so given the time, I think it's best that we leave things as they are
and continue the exploration at some future time.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add inline comments to the pg_hba_file_rules view
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Eisentraut, Daniel Gustafsson, Greg Sabino Mullane
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a "comment" column to the pg_hba_file_rules view that shows the end-of-line comment of each valid pg_hba.conf entry. The author wanted this so annotations such as tags or client names on hba entries can be read through SQL.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut objected that end-of-line comments are only one of several comment styles, so showing only them is incomplete, and that users may not want file comments exposed through a view. Daniel Gustafsson and Greg Sabino Mullane agreed. Daniel proposed agreeing on a separate annotation syntax for pg_hba.conf in a new thread, and the author withdrew the patch to start that discussion.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think we should leave file comments be file comments.  If we want some annotations to be exported to higher-level views, we should make that an intentional and explicit separate feature.

precedents_retrieved.title: Addition of authenticated ID to pg_stat_activity
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the authenticated identity, already logged by log_connections, to pg_stat_activity, with a new GUC that sets how much shared memory each backend reserves for it. After concerns about the width of pg_stat_activity, a later version moved authenticated_id and the client_* columns into a new pg_stat_connection view.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch. The thread had been idle for two months with little interest, and moving client_addr, client_hostname and client_port into a new view looked hard to justify for this feature. A reviewer also questioned the server-start GUC for truncating the value and the view's output for internal processes and Unix sockets.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This also includes a split of pg_stat_activity for client_addr, client_hostname and client_port into a new catalog, which may be hard to justify for this feature.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_hba_lookup function to get all matching pg_hba.conf entries
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a SQL function pg_hba_lookup that takes a database, a user and optionally an address and hostname, and returns the pg_hba.conf entries that match them, in match order. It replaces an earlier attempt at a catalog view of pg_hba.conf, which could not handle keywords in the database and user columns.
precedents_retrieved.objection: At the end of the last commitfest for 9.6, Tom Lane reviewed the patch and judged it not ready to commit. He found the patch too invasive in the authentication code, raised concerns about its memory management and its function signature, and found type errors in the docs. He also doubted the use case, since a user who cannot connect cannot run the function, and suggested making log_connections record the matched pg_hba line.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
And it's not very clear that it'll help
with "I can't connect", either, because if you can't connect you're
not going to be running this function.

precedents_retrieved.title: Support custom authentication methods using hooks
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds hooks in auth.c for the authentication check and for error reporting, and a pg_hba.conf method "custom" with a "provider" option, so extensions can implement authentication. The use case is checking credentials against a central external provider, such as cloud single sign-on, without syncing them into Postgres.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The commitfest manager returned the patch set because it needed author work before more review. Peter Eisentraut asked that extensions register their own method names and that built-in methods such as ldap and pam use the same interface. Stephen Frost voted -1: the hooks cover only the server side, so new methods such as OAuth still need libpq changes, and the goal stayed unclear. He also objected to a synchronous call-out during authentication.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Okay, either way you look at it, this patchset needs author work before any further review can be done.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_hba_file_settings
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a system view, first named pg_hba_file_settings and later pg_hba_rules, that shows each line of pg_hba.conf with any parse error, similar to pg_file_settings. It lets users check pg_hba.conf before a reload and shows each rule's options in a jsonb column, built with new helper functions such as push_jsonb_string_value().
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier moved it to the next CF with no reviews, then marked it returned with feedback. He questioned the use of jsonb for the options column, since the options are not nested and a simple name=value array would do. Vitaly Burovoy argued for jsonb to make filtering easier, but the thread ended without a revised patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If they were nested I'd see a case for it but it
seems to me that as presented this is just an overkill. In short, I
think that this patch needs a bit of rework, so I am marking it as
returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_stat_activity: make slow/hanging authentication more visible
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes backends report a pg_stat_activity entry in a new 'starting' state before client authentication, so connections that hang during authentication become visible. A second part adds wait events around external authentication calls (PAM, LDAP, RADIUS, SSPI, Kerberos) so DBAs can see where authentication is stuck.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The first part, the early 'starting' pg_stat_activity entry, was committed as c76db55c9085, and the author withdrew the wait-event part. Andres Freund objected that the wait events wrap regions of library code, some of which call back into Postgres (the PAM conversation callback) or can throw errors, and argued that auth methods should be made non-blocking instead. The author found the PAM handling wrong, and found that pgstat_report_activity() cannot safely replace the wait events during backend startup.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: FWIW, I continue to think that it's better to invest in making more auth methods non-blocking, rather than adding wait events for code that could maybe sometimes wait on different things internally.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add TAP test to automate the equivalent of check_guc"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add TAP test to automate the equivalent of check_guc"
Reverted commit(s): Add TAP test to automate the equivalent of check_guc
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit b0a55f4, to remove for now the TAP test that did the
equivalent of check_guc.  The test has been using pg_config --sharedir
to find the location of postgresql.conf.sample.  While the buildfarm and
normal build environments rather liked that, this proves to be an issue
for Debian where pg_config is patched to not be relocatable, causing the
test to fail.

Rather than relying on pg_config, we'd better find the sample file based
on its location from the source directory.  However, this is also an
issue as a TAP test only offers the build directory as of TESTDIR in the
environment context, so this would fail with VPATH builds.  Perhaps the
source path could be provided additionally when running the TAP tests.
Or perhaps we may be able to get away by just switching to a SQL
approach, by using PG_ABS_SRCDIR but this is going to require some extra
loops to get the sample file from the correct path in src/backend/.  In
any case, this needs more thoughts, so just revert the test case until
something better is done about this relocation problem.

roaster_notes.note: The one precedent, [P11], reverted a TAP test that broke on Debian because pg_config is patched there. It shares only the theme of TAP tests with this proposal, and its recorded reason does not apply to PAM tests or to pamconfdir. The thread cites no earlier attempt at PAM tests or a custom PAM configuration directory, so no precedent was found.

The proposal has no persistent or cross-node state: no WAL, on-disk format, catalog or wire protocol change, and nothing for pg_upgrade or standbys. The new HbaLine field changes an internal struct in a master-only feature, which raises no backpatch or extension ABI concern that I could tie to a concrete failure. The pg_hba_file_rules output gap in message #3 belongs to another angle.
pamconfdir does not grant new power: anyone who can edit pg_hba.conf can already set trust. The one gap found is the missing permission check on the PAM directory.
One objection only. Nothing in core gives a non-root DBA a custom PAM directory, so that use case gets no objection from this angle beyond its thin demand.
PAM test coverage is a project need, not a user feature, so it needs no demand evidence. The demand question applies only to the production use of pamconfdir.
